newsitem.title: USA: Lott warns Democrats not to delay funding probe.
newsitem.headline: Lott warns Democrats not to delay funding probe.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott Friday angrily accused Democrats of trying to "ambush" a Republican-led investigation into questionable White House fundraising activities.

In his first extended comments on the issue, Lott told a news conference he was "surprised and disappointed" at what he termed an "attempted ambush" by Democrats who oppose a Republican request for $6.5 million to fund the investigation.

Senate Governmental Affairs committee chairman Fred Thompson, a Tennessee Republican, Thursday tried to convince the Rules Committee to approve $6.5 million to conduct a far-reaching probe into reports of illegal foreign donations, special White House favours to donors and other activities.
Democrats, a minority in the Senate, want Thompson to scale back what they called "an unprecedented" request. The committee took no action but was expected to hold another session next week.

"There will be no more ambushes of chairman Fred Thompson. This is a responsible thing for us to do, we are going to do it," Lott said. "If they (Democrats) try a delay or a coverup strategy we will have to tell our side of the story, let the American people be the judge."

Lott accused Democrats of pushing to expand the scope of the investigation, then refusing to support the money needed to carry it out. He said he wanted to work out a solution, but maintained it could be difficult to meet Democratic requests to set a time limit on the probe.

Thompson Thursday promised an investigation into questionable financing by both parties during the 1996 election, but made clear the focus would be on Democrats. He also said he was not out to get Democratic President Clinton.
Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, a South Dakota Democrat, said Friday Democrats wanted to make sure the investigation did not "go on for years and years and years."
Noting that Thompson had already said he would need 80 investigators, Daschle said, "If he knows the number of investigators, you'd think he'd also have some sense of how much time it will take."
Republicans are five seats shy of the needed 60-vote majority to prevent a Democratic filibuster on the issue.
Thompson Thursday rejected Democratic requests to limit the duration of the investigation or to start out with an initial $1.8 million and seek more later if needed.

Once the funding hurdles are cleared, Thompson's committee plans to look into illegal or improper contributions, particularly from foreigners who gave to Democrats and who are barred from donating to U.S. campaigns in most cases.

Lott said he did not believe the American people wanted lawmakers to quibble over an "insignificant amount of money to get the job done that we are required to do when there are allegations of violations of existing laws."
